readings.title: The Massacre at Nob
readings.subtitle: Saul's Retributive Vengeance
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 22:1] And Daviḏ went from there and escaped to the cave of Aḏullam. And his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, and went down to him there.
[2] And everyone who was in distress, everyone who was in debt, and everyone bitter in being gathered to him. So he became head over them, and there were about four hundred men with him.
[3] And Daviḏ went from there to Mitspeh of Mo’aḇ and said to the sovereign of Mo’aḇ, “Please let my father and mother come here with you, till I know what <dn>Elohim</dn> does for me.”
[4] And he left them with the sovereign of Mo’aḇ, and they dwelt with him all the time that Daviḏ was in the stronghold.
[5] And the prophet Gaḏ said to Daviḏ, “Do not remain in the stronghold. Leave, and go to the land of Yehuḏah.” So Daviḏ left and went into the Ḥereth woods.
[6] And Sha’ul heard that Daviḏ and the men who were with him had been discovered, while Sha’ul was in Giḇ‛ah, sitting under a tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants standing about him.
[7] And Sha’ul said to his servants who were standing around him, “Hear now, you Binyamites! Does the son of Yishai give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make <dn>את</dn> you all commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?
[8] “For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who reveals to me that my son has made a covenant with the son of Yishai. And there is not one of you who is grieved for me or reveals to me that my son has stirred up <dn>את</dn> my servant against me, to lie in wait, as it is this day.”
[9] And Do’ěḡ the Eḏomite, who was set over the servants of Sha’ul, answered and said, “I saw <dn>את</dn> the son of Yishai going to Noḇ, to Aḥimeleḵ son of Aḥituḇ.
[10] “And he inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for him, gave him food, and gave him <dn>את</dn> the sword of Golyath the Philistine.”
[11] And the sovereign sent someone to call <dn>את</dn> Aḥimeleḵ the priest, son of Aḥituḇ, and <dn>את</dn> all his father’s house, the priests who were in Noḇ. And they all came to the sovereign,
[12] and Sha’ul said, “Hear now, son of Aḥituḇ!” And he answered, “Here I am, my master.”
[13] And Sha’ul said to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Yishai, by giving him bread and a sword, and have inquired of <dn>Elohim</dn> for him, to rise against me, to lie in wait, as it is this day?”
[14] And Aḥimeleḵ answered <dn>את</dn> the sovereign and said, “And who among all your servants is so trustworthy as Daviḏ, who is the sovereign’s son-in-law, and has turned aside to your counsel, and is esteemed in your house?
[15] “Have I today begun to inquire of <dn>Elohim</dn> for him? Far be it from me! Let not the sovereign lay a case against his servant, or against any in the house of my father. For your servant knew not of all this, little or much.”
[16] And the sovereign said, “You shall certainly die, Aḥimeleḵ, you and all your father’s house!”
[17] The sovereign then said to the guards who stood about him, “Turn and put the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to death, because their hand also is with Daviḏ, and because they knew when he fled and did not reveal it to me.” But the servants of the sovereign would not lift <dn>את</dn> their hands to come against the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[18] And the sovereign said to Do’ěḡ, “You turn and come against the priests!” So Do’ěḡ the Eḏomite turned and came against the priests, and put to death on that day eighty-five men who wore a linen shoulder garment.
[19] And he struck <dn>את</dn> Noḇ, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, from men even to women, from children even to nursing infants, and oxen and donkeys and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
[20] And one of the sons of Aḥimeleḵ son of Aḥituḇ, named Eḇyathar, escaped and fled after Daviḏ.
[21] And Eḇyathar reported to Daviḏ that Sha’ul had killed <dn>את</dn> the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[22] And Daviḏ said to Eḇyathar, “I knew that day, when Do’ěḡ the Eḏomite was there, that he would certainly inform Sha’ul. I am accountable for all the lives of your father’s house.
[23] “Remain with me, do not fear. For he who seeks <dn>את</dn> my life seeks <dn>את</dn> your life, but with me you are safe.”

readings.title: The Gathering of the Mighty Men
readings.subtitle: The Army of Elohim Assembles

readings.title: The Deliverance of Qe'ilah
readings.subtitle: David's Escape to the Wilderness
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 23:1] And they informed Daviḏ, saying, “See, the Philistines are fighting against Qe‛ilah, and they are plundering <dn>את</dn> the threshing-floors.”
[2] So Daviḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Shall I go and strike these Philistines?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Daviḏ, <dq>“Go and smite the Philistines, and save <dn>את</dn> Qe‛ilah.”</dq>
[3] And Daviḏ’s men said to him, “See, we here in Yehuḏah are afraid. How much more, then, if we go to Qe‛ilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
[4] And Daviḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> once again. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered him and said, <dq>“Arise, go down to Qe‛ilah, for <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> the Philistines into your hand.”</dq>
[5] So Daviḏ and his men went to Qe‛ilah and fought with the Philistines, and he led away <dn>את</dn> their livestock and struck them, a great smiting. Thus Daviḏ saved <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Qe‛ilah.
[6] And it came to be, when Eḇyathar son of Aḥimeleḵ fled to Daviḏ at Qe‛ilah, that he went down with a shoulder garment in his hand.
[7] And Sha’ul was informed that Daviḏ had gone to Qe‛ilah. Then Sha’ul said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has estranged him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town that has gates and bars.”
[8] And Sha’ul summoned <dn>את</dn> all the people to battle, to go down to Qe‛ilah to besiege Daviḏ and his men.
[9] And Daviḏ knew that Sha’ul was plotting evil against him, and said to Eḇyathar the priest, “Bring the shoulder garment here.”
[10] And Daviḏ said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, Your servant has heard for certain that Sha’ul seeks to come to Qe‛ilah to destroy the city for my sake.
[11] “Are the landowners of Qe‛ilah going to surrender me into his hand? Is Sha’ul coming down, as Your servant has heard? O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, I pray, let Your servant know.” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“He is coming down.”</dq>
[12] And Daviḏ said, “Are the landowners of Qe‛ilah going to surrender me and my men into the hand of Sha’ul?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“They are going to surrender you.”</dq>
[13] Then Daviḏ and his men, about six hundred, arose and left Qe‛ilah and went wherever they could go. And Sha’ul was informed that Daviḏ had escaped from Qe‛ilah, and he ceased to go out.
[14] And Daviḏ remained in the wilderness, in strongholds, and remained in the hill country in the Wilderness of Ziph. And Sha’ul sought him every day, but <dn>Elohim</dn> did not give him into his hand.
[15] And Daviḏ saw that Sha’ul had come out to seek <dn>את</dn> his life while Daviḏ was in the Wilderness of Ziph at Ḥoresh.
[16] And Yehonathan, Sha’ul’s son, arose and went to Daviḏ at Ḥoresh and strengthened <dn>את</dn> his hand in <dn>Elohim</dn>,
[17] and said to him, “Do not fear, for the hand of Sha’ul my father is not going to find you, and you are to reign over Yisra’ěl, and I am to be next to you. Even my father Sha’ul knows that.”
[18] And they made a covenant before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Daviḏ remained at Ḥoresh while Yehonathan went to his own house.
[19] And the Ziphites came up to Sha’ul at Giḇ‛ah, saying, “Is Daviḏ not hiding with us in strongholds Ḥoresh, in the hill of Ḥaḵilah, which is on the south of the wasteland?
[20] “And now, O sovereign, by all the desire of your being, come down, come down, and our part is to surrender him into the sovereign’s hand.”
[21] And Sha’ul said, “Blessed are you of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for you have sympathy with me.
[22] “Please go, prepare yet further and find out and see <dn>את</dn> the place where his hide-out is, who has seen him there. For I am told that he is very cunning.
[23] “So look, and learn all about the hiding places where he hides. And you shall come back to me with certainty, then I shall go with you. And it shall be, if he is in the land, that I shall search for him throughout all the clans of Yehuḏah.”
[24] And they rose up and went to Ziph before Sha’ul, while Daviḏ and his men were in the Wilderness of Ma‛on, in the desert plain on the south of the wasteland.
[25] And Sha’ul and his men went to seek him, and they informed Daviḏ, so he went down to the rock, and remained in the Wilderness of Ma‛on. And when Sha’ul heard this, he pursued Daviḏ in the Wilderness of Ma‛on.
[26] And Sha’ul went on one side of the mountain, and Daviḏ and his men on the other side of the mountain. And Daviḏ was hurrying to get away from Sha’ul, for Sha’ul and his men were surrounding Daviḏ and his men to take them.
[27] Then a messenger came to Sha’ul, saying, “Hurry and come, for the Philistines have invaded the land!”
[28] So Sha’ul turned back from pursuing Daviḏ, and went against the Philistines. Therefore they called that place Sela Hammaḥleqoth.
[29] And Daviḏ went up from there and remained in strongholds at Ěn Geḏi.

readings.title: A Cry from the Cave
readings.subtitle: Taking Refuge in the Shadow of His Wings
readings.text:
[Psalm 57:1] Show me favour, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, show me favour! For in <dn>You</dn> my being is taking refuge; And in the shadow of <dn>Your</dn> wings I take refuge, Until destruction passes by.
[2] I cry out to the Most High <dn>Elohim</dn>, To <dn>Ěl</dn> who is perfecting all matters for me.
[3] <dn>He</dn> sends from the heavens and saves me; <dn>He</dn> reproaches the one who would swallow me up. Selah. <dn>Elohim</dn> sends forth <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment and <dn>His</dn> truth.
[4] My being is in the midst of lions; I lie among those who breathe fire, Whose teeth are spears and arrows, And their tongue is a sharp sword.
[5] Be exalted, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, above the heavens; Let <dn>Your</dn> esteem be above all the earth.
[6] They have prepared a net for my footsteps; My being was bowed down; They have dug a pit before me; They fell into the midst of it! Selah.
[7] My heart is firm, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, My heart is firm; I sing and praise.
[8] Awake, my esteem! Awake, harp and lyre! I awake the dawn.
[9] I praise <dn>You</dn> among the peoples, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; I sing to <dn>You</dn> among the nations.
[10] For <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment is great up to the heavens, And <dn>Your</dn> truth unto the clouds.
[11] Be exalted above the heavens, O <dn>Elohim</dn>; Let <dn>Your</dn> esteem be above all the earth.

readings.title: A Complaint Poured Out
readings.subtitle: The Plea of the Persecuted
readings.text:
[Psalm 142:1] I cry out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with my voice; I pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with my voice.
[2] I pour out my complaint before <dn>Him</dn>; I declare before <dn>Him</dn> my distress.
[3] When my spirit grew faint within me, Then <dn>You</dn> know my path. In the way in which I walk They have hidden a trap for me.
[4] Look to the right hand and see, And no one is concerned for me; No refuge remains to me; No one inquires after my being.
[5] I cried out to <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: I said, “<dn>You</dn> are my refuge, My portion in the land of the living.
[6] “Listen to my cry, For I am brought very low; Deliver me from my persecutors, For they are too strong for me.
[7] “Bring my being out of prison, To give thanks to <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Name. Let the righteous gather around me, Because <dn>You</dn> deal kindly with me.”

readings.title: The Doom of the Deceitful
readings.subtitle: Trusting in the Loving-Commitment of Elohim
readings.text:
[Psalm 52:1] Why do you boast in evil, O mighty man? The loving-commitment of <dn>Ěl</dn> is all day long!
[2] Your tongue devises destruction, Like a sharp razor, working deceit.
[3] You loved evil more than good, Lying more than speaking righteousness. Selah.
[4] You loved all devouring words, O tongue of deceit.
[5] Let <dn>Ěl</dn> also break you down forever, Take you and pluck you out of your tent. And <dn>He</dn> shall uproot you From the land of the living. Selah.
[6] And let the righteous see and fear, And laugh at him, saying,
[7] “See the man who did not make <dn>Elohim</dn> his strength, But trusted in his many riches, Being strong in his destruction.”
[8] But I am like a green olive tree In the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, I have trusted in the loving-commitment of <dn>Elohim</dn> Forever and ever.
[9] I thank <dn>You</dn> forever, Because <dn>You</dn> have done it; And in the presence of <dn>Your</dn> lovingly-committed ones I wait on <dn>Your</dn> Name, for it is good.
